questionText:

"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

What critical chronological error did Alexander Cunningham make when attempting to date Harappan artefacts?

options.text: He dated them to the European Middle Ages

options.text: He considered them to be modern forgeries made by railway workers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: He tried to fit Harappan seals within the time-frame of early historic cities (6th c. BCE to 4th c. CE) known from Chinese pilgrim chronicles
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: He believed they were manufactured in 18th-century Bengal
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Cunningham relied on records of Chinese Buddhist pilgrims (Faxian and Xuanzang) and assumed Indian urbanization began in the 6th century BCE, missing Harappa's 3rd millennium BCE antiquity.
